issues.detail: The Chinese renders 'וְלֵךְ אֶֽשְׁלָחֲךָ' as '去我那裡差遣你' ('go to me, I will send you'), which adds '我那裡' (to me) not present in the Hebrew. The Hebrew simply says 'go, I will send you' (וְלֵךְ אֶֽשְׁלָחֲךָ), meaning 'go, for I will send you' or 'go, I will send you' — the 'to me' is an addition that changes the sense of the command.
